about: Solomon re-enters Jerusalem and weeps with the elders and Zadok over the Ark's departure. His counsellors console him: Zion stays or goes by God's will and her own, as the Ark's history already showed among the Philistines (Dagon, the plague, the Philistine gold, the two animals and the cart), under Samuel, Saul and David. They end by reminding him that the wisdom God gave him is his own and that fools' words cannot harm it.

sentences.i: Then he entered the city of Jerusalem and wept there too, together with the elders of Jerusalem, weeping greatly within the house of God.
sentences.n: ወእምዝ 'and-after-this'. አተወ 'he entered' (G perfect) with the place as direct object, ሀገረ is construct 'city-of'. በህየኒ = በ-ህየ 'in there' + enclitic -ኒ 'also'. አእሩገ is construct plural 'elders-of' (አእሩግ, plural of አረጋዊ 'old man, elder'). ብካየ ዐቢየ 'great weeping' is a cognate accusative (the noun of the verb በከየ, as in the published ብካየ መሪረ). ቤተ እግዚኣብሔር is the Temple Solomon built. Solomon comes back from the pursuit of the Ethiopians (chs. 57–58) to a Jerusalem without the Ark.

sentences.i: After that the king and Zadok the priest clasped one another by the neck and wept bitterly in the place where Zion had sat; and after a long while (?) they fell silent.
sentences.n: ተኣኀዙ is 3mp of ተኣኀዘ, the reflexive/reciprocal stem 'take hold of one another', so the plural verb covers 'king ... with Zadok'. ክሳውዲሆሙ 'their necks' is my reading of an irregular plural of ክሳድ 'neck' (?). መሪረ 'bitterly' is an adverbial accusative. ምንባሪሃ ለጽዮን 'her seat, of Zion' (anticipatory pronoun + ለ, the usual way to mark a genitive after a suffixed noun): the Ark's resting-place in the Temple. ወአርመሙ 'they fell silent' (አርመመ). ጒንዱይ ሰዐት 'a lingering hour' = 'a long while' (?): ጒንዱይ is glossed as the noun 'lingering, delay' in the published entry (here qualifying ሰዐት); since እምድኅረ is 'after', the silence follows the long weeping. Zadok the priest is the high priest of Solomon's day.

sentences.i: Then the elders rose and spoke to the king, saying, 'Do not grieve, our lord, over this matter. We know that Zion stays nowhere except where God wishes, from first to last, and nothing happens except by God's will;
sentences.n: መላህቅት is a plural noun I take as 'elders, leading men' (?), related to ልሕቀ 'grow great'; the sense is a council of senior men consoling the king. ወተናገርዎ ለንጉሥ: verb + -ዎ 'him', then ለ- again marks the person addressed. እንዘ ይብሉ 'while saying' introduces direct speech. ኢትሕዝን 2ms jussive 'do not grieve'. በእንተዝ = በእንተ + ዝ 'concerning this'. ዘእንበለ ኀበ ፈቀደ 'except to-where he wished'. ኢትነብር ጽዮን: Zion (the Ark) is feminine; ነብረ 'sit, dwell'. ወአልቦ ዘይከውን 'there is none/nothing that happens'. The theology of the Ark's free movement is the core of this chapter.

sentences.l: And-concerning-Zion-also, earlier, in-days-of Eli priest, before they-asked our-fathers a-king, led-her-captive the-Philistines in-midst the-camp, when turned-from(?)-them God Israel in-midst battle, and-fell her-priests Hophni and-Phinehas by-mouth-of iron, and-took-her the-Philistines, Ark-of his-law of-God, and-brought-her into their-land and-put-her in-midst house-of their-god Dagon;
sentences.i: And as for Zion too, long ago, in the days of Eli the priest, before our fathers asked for a king, the Philistines carried her off in the midst of the camp, when God turned away from Israel (?) in the battle: her priests Hophni and Phinehas fell by the edge of the sword, and the Philistines took the Ark of God's law, brought it into their own land, and set it in the house of their god Dagon;
sentences.n: Allusion to 1 Samuel 4–5: Eli, his sons Hophni and Phinehas, the Philistines (ኢሎፍሊ, from the Septuagint's Greek allophyloi 'foreigners') and Dagon. ዘበእንተ ጽዮንሂ 'what concerns Zion also' (-ሂ enclitic). ዘእንበለ ይስአሉ 'before they asked' (ዘእንበለ + subjunctive 'before'), ንጉሠ 'a king' accusative (1 Samuel 8). ፄወውዋ 'they carried her off captive' (ፄወወ 'take captive') + -ዋ 'her'. ትዕይንት 'camp, battle-array'. ተሀየዮሙ: root and sense uncertain (?); I keep the house reading 'turned away from' (chs. 30, 60), with ለእስራኤል naming Israel. በአፈ ኀጺን 'by the mouth of iron' = by the sword (Hebrew idiom). ለታቦተ: ለ- marks the object, ታቦተ is construct 'Ark-of'; ሕጉ ለእግዚኣብሔር 'his law, God's' is a resumptive genitive. Dagon is the Philistine god.

sentences.i: Dagon was broken and destroyed and became like dust (?); their land turned to desert through the mice (?), which ate all the produce of their land; and their own bodies too became ulcerous and swollen (?);
sentences.n: Allusion to 1 Samuel 5–6 (Dagon fallen, the plague of tumours, the mice). ተሰብረ ወተሀጒለ 'was broken and was destroyed' are reflexive/passive (ተ-) forms. ጸበል: I read 'dust, ashes' (?). በድወ 'desert' (በድው), predicate of ኮነት. The printed words በአና ፡ ጹት are broken: ጹት stands alone. The same word appears whole at unit 13 as አናጹት, so I read 'by mice' (?), with 'አና ጹት' kept exactly as printed. ወበልዐ 'and it devoured' is masculine singular, subject apparently the mice (collective). ጸልዐ and ሕበጠ read as accusative nouns (ጸልዕ 'ulcer', ሕበጥ 'swelling', as in units 6 and 13; the accusative ends in -ä), both predicates of ኮነ: 'became an ulcer and a swelling' (?).

sentences.i: We are not to send her away empty-handed (?); give her a fringe-offering (?), so that this sin of yours may be forgiven and your affliction lightened once Zion has returned to her city. If you do not send her back to her city, her staying with you will not be good, but all of you will be scourged until you are finished.'
sentences.n: ዕራቃ 'naked, bare', adverbial: 'empty-handed' (?). ዘንፌንዋ is 1cp ('that we send her'): the priests include themselves, 'we are not to send her away empty-handed', then turn to the kings with the imperative ሀብዋ. ሞጻ keeps its house reading 'fringe (?)' (chs. 51–52, 55–56, where the Philistines' gold is tied to Zion's fringe), so ሀብዋ ሞጻ is 'give her fringe(-gold)', the guilt-offering of 1 Samuel 6:3–4 (?). ትስረይ 'be forgiven' (ሰረየ), ትሰስል 'be eased' (ሰሰለ, 'loosened, lightened'). ሶበ ... ወሶበሰ 'when ... but if'. ኢኮነ ሠናየ 'it would not be good'. The final tokens ተኀል ፡ ቁ are broken in the source: it is plainly ተኀልቁ 'you are finished/perish' (ኀልቀ), printed as two words, kept as printed.

sentences.i: The priests (?) of the Philistines took counsel again and said to their kings and governors, 'Make for her, for the heads of your households (?), a fringe-offering (?) of gold: eight images of mice, as they ruined your land, and eight images of a man's body, as you were sick in your bodies with ulcer and swelling in your hindquarters (?).'
sentences.n: Allusion to 1 Samuel 6:4–5 (golden tumours and golden mice). The text prints ፰ 'eight' twice, where 1 Samuel 6:4 has five of each; kept as printed. አናጹት 'mice' (?) is the whole form of the broken ጹት above. ወርቀ ሞጻ 'gold, fringe (?)' (house reading of ሞጻ, see unit 11). አጥፍኡ 'they destroyed' (አጥፍአ). ነፍስተ ብእሲ 'person-of a man' in the accusative construct. ሐመምክሙ 'you were sick' (2mp), with ነፍስተክሙ 'your persons' as accusative of respect: 'you were sick in your persons'. In በርእሰ አብያቲክሙ 'at the head of your houses' I am unsure of the intended sense (?). ቊልፈትክሙ: I am not sure of the word (?); it is the part of the body affected, probably 'hindquarters', fitting the biblical 'secret parts'.

sentences.l: And-said-to-them again the-diviners of-the-Philistines: Let-them-bring two she-camels(?) which have-borne-firstborn at one time, and-let-them-load(?) carts upon-them, and-let-them-shut their-young in-a-house, and-let-them-yoke them, let-them-leave them, let-them-go where they-wish;
sentences.i: The Philistine diviners said again, 'Let them bring two she-camels (?) that have both borne their first young at the same time (?), and let them harness carts to them (?); let them hold back their young and shut them in a house, yoke the animals, leave them, and let them go where they wish.
sentences.n: Allusion to 1 Samuel 6:7–9 (the cart and the nursing cows). Here the animals are ናቃት, which I take as 'she-camels' (cf. Arabic nāqa) (?), and they are called አግማል 'camels' afterward (unit 19); the biblical cows are not named in this text. ተበኵራ 'have borne firstborn' (ተበኵረ). ይርሐኑ: root unclear (?); the sense 'load/hitch' is from context. እጐላቲሆሙ 'their young'. ይዕጽዉ 'let them shut'. ይፅምድዎን 'let them yoke them' (ጸምደ 'bind, yoke'). The jussives ይኅድግዎን and ይሖራ continue the list without ወ.

sentences.i: If they go straight to Jerusalem, then we shall know that God has had mercy on our land; but if they balk (?) and turn aside (?) and want to go back after their young, then we shall know that God is angry with us and has not withdrawn his scourge until he destroys us and our land.'

sentences.i: Later, when your father had put things right (?) and reigned over Israel, he took her from the city of Samaria and brought her here to Jerusalem, dancing (?) before her on his feet and clapping (?) his hands for joy of her, since she had risen for him to come to the city of David your father.
sentences.n: 2 Samuel 6 (David brings the Ark up, dancing). The text says ሀገረ ሰማርያ 'city of Samaria' where the biblical place is Kiriath-jearim/Obed-edom's house; Samaria was built later, so this is the book's own wording, kept as printed. አርትዐ 'he became upright / set right' (?). ያፅሕስ 'he danced' (?) and ይጠፍሕ 'he clapped' (?): both roots are uncertain to me and I follow the biblical scene. እስመ ተንሥአት ሎቱ 'for she rose for him', i.e. she consented to go. ከመ ትምጻእ ሀገረ ዳዊት 'that she come (to) the city-of David'.

sentences.i: As for what you say about Zion having gone to their city in the land of Ethiopia: if God wished it, and she herself wished it, no one can hinder her, not even one; for she goes by her own will and returns by her own will, if God is pleased.
sentences.n: ዘትብል 'which you say' (2ms), Solomon's lament; the comforters now answer it. በእንተ ዘሖረት 'about that she went' (ሖረ). sentences.l: For alien to-wisdom like a-lamp to-the-sun, which does-not-avail, and-like milk(?) and-ዕጒስታር(?) to-honey does-not-avail; likewise the-words-of fools against a-wise-man does-not-avail, like smoke to-the-eye and-like ቆዕ(?) to-teeth, likewise does-not-avail against a-wise-man the-speech-of fools.
sentences.i: For folly (?) is foreign to wisdom, as a lamp is to the sun, which is of no use; and as milk (?) and ዕጒስታር (?) are to honey, of no use: likewise the words of fools against a wise man are of no use, like smoke to the eye and ቆዕ (?) to the teeth. So the speech of fools does not avail against a wise man.
sentences.n: Proverbial close, with a parallel in Proverbs 10:26 (smoke to the eyes, something sour to the teeth). ነኪር 'foreign, alien'; ለጥበብ 'to wisdom'; I take the unstated subject as folly (?). ከመ ማኅቶት ለፀሐይ 'like a lamp to the sun'. ዘኢይበቊዕ 'which does not avail' (በቊዐ 'avail, be of use'); ኢይበቊዕ negates the likeness. ብሒእ 'milk' (?) and ዕጒስታር: I cannot identify these two words (?); I give 'milk' tentatively, and ዕጒስታር is left in Geʿez. ቆዕ is also uncertain (?), perhaps 'something sour'. ጢስ 'smoke', ዐይን 'eye', ስነን 'teeth'. ነገሮሙ ለአብዳን 'words-of them, of the fools' (resumptive ለ-). The closing ፨ run is the chapter-end mark, attached to this unit and kept as printed.
